races.name: Watch On Racing TV Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Sudbury Hill
runners_data.note: Progressive flat stayer making the switch to hurdles with Harry Derham; placed twice over 2m at Goodwood on good ground and won over 17f, so the trip and surface suit; genuine hold-up style means he needs Wicksey to have done enough by the last to get rolling, which is plausible given the likely tempo.
runners_data.comment: Took a maiden hurdle at Newton Abbot by 22 lengths last time, an emphatic display at around 2m on good ground; carrying a penalty just six days on, he rates a live threat, though the quick turnaround is a query.

runners_data.name: Tiny Riot
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's yard is flying (12/24 in 14 days) and Harry Skelton gives this pair serious tactical clout; placed over 2m on good at Haydock and won at 2m, so the trip-going combination looks ideal; true hold-up horse who should get a good sight of the race from a handy position if Skelton elects to chase Wicksey.
runners_data.comment: Keen-going in front at Market Rasen last time, he spent his energy too freely and was beaten 8½l under penalty, but the talent is clear; effective around 2m on good ground with a yard in outstanding form, he looks the one to beat with improvement to come.

runners_data.name: Lucky Sevens
runners_data.note: Won twice on good ground at 10f on the flat and ran creditably at 12f; naturally races from the rear but, with the field stacked with hold-up types, getting his preferred deep berth will be difficult — discounted slightly as a result; Jonathan Burke is capable of adapting, but this redistribution is a genuine tactical complication.
runners_data.comment: Successful in a Flat handicap at Brighton last time, he makes his hurdles debut for a capable yard and that Flat form suggests some ability; a largely unknown quantity over obstacles, he ranks fifth on our figures, so a gentle introduction would be no surprise.

runners_data.name: Serragasso
runners_data.note: Clare Hobson's runner arrives on a long absence (95 days, flat form), has struggled with stamina in finishes on previous starts, and while a natural hold-up horse, is unlikely to land in a true rear-running slot given the race shape — all three factors combine to make this one of the harder-to-fancy runners in the field.
runners_data.comment: Down the field in a Flat handicap at Southwell on his racecourse debut, he tackles hurdles for the first time off a short break; with little to work with on form and ranking last on our figures, he faces a stiff task here.

runners_data.name: Wicksey
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's sole confirmed front-runner who won back-to-back over 12f at Stratford and has the course form that matters; his prominent style is his strongest asset today, giving McLernon total control of the race from the front; modest trainer 14-day stats (3/22) are worth noting but the tactical advantage of unchallenged lead is significant.
runners_data.comment: Second beaten 4¼l at Redcar over 14f on the Flat last time, performing to his level, he looks the profile to make a capable hurdler; the switch to obstacles and today’s 16f trip are both unknowns, but he carries potential and could go well.

runners_data.name: High Aura
runners_data.note: Unknown quantity on debut for Dan Skelton's powerful yard; running style unclassified, going unknown, and lightly raced — carries less weight (147lbs) than rivals which could offset inexperience; Tristan Durrell takes the ride and the Skelton operation consistently produces well-schooled hurdling debutants worth monitoring in-running.
runners_data.comment: By Too Darn Hot, with a dam effective at 12f-14f and a half-sister to a 2m4f stayer in the family, the pedigree offers stamina hope for this trip; from a trainer in fine form, she commands interest on debut, though she may be the yard’s second string.

races.paceDynamic: Wicksey is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate terms from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground over this 2m½f trip at Stratford. That uncontested pace-setting role creates a flat, even tempo that is likely to compress the field and minimise the advantage of a late finish, favouring horses who can travel prominently and pounce from a handy position. Sudbury Hill and Tiny Riot are the most credible closers with genuine hold-up credentials, while Lucky Sevens and Serragasso — both natural hold-up horses — have been pushed into the midfield mapping because this field holds more come-from-behind types than the race shape can accommodate in true rear positions, meaning they are unlikely to enjoy their preferred tactical berth. The race shape strongly favours a horse who can sit just off Wicksey's uncontested lead and produce a fluid jumping display, picking off the front-runner approaching the final flight under the fast ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wicksey controls, closers ambush
scenarios.trigger: If Wicksey bowls along unchallenged and sets a fair but not punishing tempo, allowing a prominent-tracking horse to collar him late.
scenarios.body: If Wicksey bowls along unchallenged and sets a fair but not punishing tempo, allowing a prominent-tracking horse to collar him late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Wicksey front-runs, holds on
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is even gentler than expected and no chaser has the pace to reel in a well-jumped front-runner on this fast surface.
scenarios.body: If the tempo is even gentler than expected and no chaser has the pace to reel in a well-jumped front-runner on this fast surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses land late
scenarios.trigger: If Wicksey goes off too fast or makes an error, stringing the field out and setting up a genuine staying test from three out.
scenarios.body: If Wicksey goes off too fast or makes an error, stringing the field out and setting up a genuine staying test from three out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — errors unsettle race
scenarios.trigger: If jumping mistakes by Wicksey disrupt the pace-setting plan and reshuffle the field mid-race.
scenarios.body: If jumping mistakes by Wicksey disrupt the pace-setting plan and reshuffle the field mid-race.

watchPoints.text: Watch Wicksey's jumping throughout — any error at a hurdle will remove the race's only pace anchor and completely reshape what follows, directly boosting horses positioned just behind.

Lucky Sevens and Serragasso are both natural hold-up horses crowded into midfield by the race shape; if they fail to adapt and get caught in traffic turning for home, their chances evaporate even if the form says they should be competitive.

High Aura is a complete unknown — Skelton debutants can be well-schooled and lightly raced juveniles sometimes show unexpected jumping talent; watch the market moves before the off for any indication of stable confidence.

The good-to-firm ground (confirmed for this race in the going report) is a significant leveller — horses with flat-racing form on fast surfaces (Sudbury Hill, Tiny Riot, Lucky Sevens) hold an edge in ground suitability over those whose form is mainly on softer or artificial surfaces.

races.name: Visit racingtv.com Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Juan Bermudez
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner here with strong Good-ground form (2W5P in similar conditions) and recent course-winning evidence; wears tongue-strap/cheekpieces and has been used prominently throughout his career, though STYLE_FIT flags he may not be operating at full comfort in a role where he must lead without cover — his chance is real but conditional on a generous pace not materialising.
runners_data.comment: Front-running and effective at Stratford, he took a handicap here last time by a length — benefiting from a positive ride over this trip — off a mark 3lb lower; well suited by these conditions and back in form, he is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Katherine
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up operator who has been placed once in 15 runs at similar pace but carries a long losing run (form: 8-7749) and a 7lb-claiming apprentice in the saddle; softer ground suits marginally better, though Good-to-Firm here is within range, and she must sharpen up considerably on recent efforts.
runners_data.comment: Down the field at Roscommon last time, hampered late and out of her element on soft ground, today’s better surface offers some relief; handles around 2m, but a strong run of form in recent starts is absent and the first-time cheekpieces will need to make a marked difference.

runners_data.name: Uhtred Ragnarson
runners_data.note: A five-year-old hold-up type with a win at 16f on Good ground and a solid recent placing, trained by Alan King whose yard shows 2/29 in the 14-day window; 45 days off the track is worth monitoring on seasonal fitness grounds, but his profile fits this steady-tempo shape well.
runners_data.comment: His Aintree flop is best excused as a likely fitness run, and earlier form over 2m on sound ground tells a different story; back on conditions that suit, he rates a solid threat, though 45 days between runs remains the key query.

runners_data.name: Pahlavi
runners_data.note: Genuinely a rear-of-field operator whose true running style is hold-up — mapped to midfield here solely because the field is stacked with similar types — and his trainer John Joseph Hanlon is 2/29 in the past fortnight; consistent without winning in similar going (14/15 sim-going runs), he lacks a killer punch but is dependable for a place.
runners_data.comment: Suited by 2m on good ground and these conditions look right, but his Southwell effort last time — well held at the finish despite keeping tabs — underlines he needs improvement to land this; the first-time tongue-tie could sharpen things.

runners_data.name: Reteti
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse shifted to midfield on the pace map due to field congestion at the rear; Marc Goldstein rides and the horse has four placed efforts in five recent runs without winning, showing admirable consistency — his Good-ground record (3W, multiple places) is solid and the style fits if he can deliver his effort cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Third at Plumpton most recently, unable to sustain the early pace but plugging on to finish 4¼l back, he remains in fair nick over 2m on good ground; the first-time hood adds interest but he faces a stiff task on our figures.

runners_data.name: Playful Fox
runners_data.note: Youngest runner at four years old, trained by Dan Skelton (11/26 in last 14 days — a live yard flag) with Harry Skelton aboard; a true hold-up type reassigned to midfield on the map, his two career placings include a second at 16f on Good and he showed ability before an unseating; the Skelton combination and trainer form are the most compelling engagement here.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with promise at Worcester last time before flattening out late, the suspicion being that 2m4f stretched him; dropping to 2m here should play to his strengths, and with the trainer in strong form and the tongue-tie added, he commands respect despite being yet to score.

races.paceDynamic: Juan Bermudez is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, he is set to bowl along at his own rhythm on good-to-firm ground at Stratford over 2m½f — an unchallenged, sustainable gallop rather than a pressured slog. Katherine, Uhtred Ragnarson, Pahlavi, Reteti, and Playful Fox are all natural hold-up or rear-of-field horses, meaning the pace Juan Bermudez sets will be uncontested and metronomic, creating a steady tempo that keeps the race well within his control deep into the back straight. This shape strongly favours hold-up and late-finishing profiles — horses that can travel comfortably off a single honest pace and produce one clean finishing effort — but the redistribution note is critical: Pahlavi, Reteti, and Playful Fox are genuine hold-up operators who have been mapped to midfield purely because the map cannot accommodate five hold-up horses at the rear simultaneously, and their actual tactical positions in running are likely to be towards the back as normal. The race therefore shapes as a controlled-tempo, single-pacemaker contest where the winner is most likely to emerge from those hold-up horses launching off Juan Bermudez's back in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bermudez Dictates, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Juan Bermudez controls a steady, uncontested gallop throughout and the hold-up horses get a clean run turning for home.
scenarios.body: If Juan Bermudez controls a steady, uncontested gallop throughout and the hold-up horses get a clean run turning for home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Bermudez Steals It Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Juan Bermudez slows the pace sufficiently that the field is lulled into complacency and he kicks clear before hold-up horses can organise a response.
scenarios.body: If Juan Bermudez slows the pace sufficiently that the field is lulled into complacency and he kicks clear before hold-up horses can organise a response.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swamp The Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady enough that multiple hold-up runners produce finishing runs simultaneously and the race becomes a blanket sprint to the line.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely steady enough that multiple hold-up runners produce finishing runs simultaneously and the race becomes a blanket sprint to the line.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Form Reversal
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo collapses entirely and the hold-up horses fail to make meaningful headway, handing the race to a well-positioned prominent runner.
scenarios.body: If the tempo collapses entirely and the hold-up horses fail to make meaningful headway, handing the race to a well-positioned prominent runner.

watchPoints.text: Watch Playful Fox: the Skelton yard's 11/26 strike rate in the past 14 days combined with Harry Skelton's tactical awareness could make this horse a significant threat if he gets the run of the race from his hold-up position in the straight.

Watch Juan Bermudez's pace judgement leaving the back straight — if he quickens too early and sets a genuinely strong tempo, he risks emptying before the last and handing it to the hold-up horses; if he dawdles, he retains control.

Watch Uhtred Ragnarson's fitness coming into this off 45 days absent — Alan King's runners can need a run after a break, and any greenness turning in could compromise his finishing effort despite the style suiting perfectly.

Watch for traffic issues in the straight: with five hold-up horses converging on one pacemaker, crowding risks at the final hurdle are elevated — clean passage will be a key differentiator between the closers.

Watch the actual in-running positions of Pahlavi and Reteti — both are true hold-up horses likely to drop to the rear despite their midfield map placement, and any failure to get cover could cause them to race less efficiently than their form suggests.

races.name: Sun Racing The Home Of Racing Novices' Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Catchim
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a course win on similar good ground and a competitive recent form string; Charles & Adam Pogson yard in quiet patch (0/4 over 14 days), but James Bowen is strong in the finish and the 16-17f runs suggest 2m3½f at Stratford is on the outer edge of ideal stamina.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and effective up to 2m4f on good and soft, he performed to his level last time when second beaten 6½l by a well-handicapped rival off 99 — just 1lb higher here, he rates a solid each-way threat.

runners_data.name: A Little Something
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with two course wins at 20f on good ground and strong recent form (PP22-11); Emma Lavelle 0/4 in 14 days, but Ben Jones rides well here — the solo lead role at a sustainable gallop is the critical asset and the going is exactly what it wants.
runners_data.comment: Consecutive victories have her building momentum, handling this trip and ground effectively; her latest success was authoritative — 12 lengths clear off a mark 11lb lower — and now chasing a treble, the form reads well for her chances here.

runners_data.name: White Riot
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over 16f on good ground at Stratford and has Fergal O'Brien in fine form (3/25); the recent run of F4 hints at some jumping fragility at chase fences, and the step up to 2m3½f from prior starts at 2m is a stamina query worth watching.
runners_data.comment: Struggling to make his mark over hurdles, he was beaten 41 lengths in a novice contest at Uttoxeter last time and the pattern of falls and pulled ups gives little confidence; handles 2m on good ground but needs a dramatic upturn to feature here.

runners_data.name: Gore Point
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent horse with five places from five starts including two seconds on good ground at 20f; Sam Twiston-Davies is an obvious booking upgrade and tongue-tie is worn — the slightly lower OR of 96 versus the 100-rated pair gives a small weight advantage that counts on fast ground.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in placing and comfortable on this trip and going, the first-time tongue-tie is an interesting addition to help sharpen his closing effort; Fontwell was a run compromised by jumping lapses and probably served as a prep, so a livelier showing is on the cards.

runners_data.name: Kings Order
runners_data.note: Lightly exposed five-year-old whose form figures (P706-5) reveal no wins and modest placings, with all best efforts on softer ground — the good-to-firm conditions here are an obvious concern; tongue-tie worn, and 149lbs is the lightest weight in the field, but the going and form-class gap make him difficult to fancy.
runners_data.comment: Well held at Worcester last time and yet to show much promise under rules, he sits at the foot of the field on our figures; the first-time tongue-tie offers a possible angle but a substantial turnaround in form looks required.

runners_data.name: No Mean Feat
runners_data.note: Progressive-looking handicapper in maiden company whose natural rear-of-field style is squeezed into a midfield slot by the race shape; the 54-day absence is notable, headgear (visor) is a flag, and 0/5 for Simon Hodgson in the past fortnight — the combined headwinds are significant.
runners_data.comment: Fresh from a wind operation and now fitted with first-time cheekpieces, there are reasons for positivity; fourth at Fontwell last time off a light weight, he handles this trip, though 54 days off means fitness remains to be confirmed.

runners_data.name: Citizen Jane
runners_data.note: A true hold-up mare whose entire recent form was compiled on soft ground — all five recent starts came on soft-to-heavy, making the good-to-firm conditions here a genuine question mark; the 807-day absence (last run 43 starts ago in point terms) adds further uncertainty, and the natural closer style is hemmed in by this pace shape.
runners_data.comment: A points winner at 3m suggesting jumping ability, she was well beaten in her latest point outing and returns off a long absence; the first-time hood is a possible aid but she needs to find a great deal more here.

races.paceDynamic: A Little Something is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival willing to match strides from the front, is set to bowl along at a sustainable gallop and control tempo throughout the 2m3½f trip on good-to-firm ground at Stratford. Gore Point, White Riot and, to a lesser degree, Catchim will likely sit just off the leader in a compact group, meaning the race will be run at a measured but consistent pace rather than a searching test. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — No Mean Feat and Citizen Jane are genuine closers who are effectively crowded into a midfield position in this shape, meaning neither will get the true patient run that suits them best. This configuration — a lone, uncontested leader at a controlled gallop — heavily favours prominent racers who can travel smoothly just behind the pace and pounce from a strong position turning in; genuine hold-up horses needing a truly fast tempo to unleash a late run are structurally disadvantaged.

scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If A Little Something dictates at a steady clip and the race truly develops into a one-pace test from the front.
scenarios.body: If A Little Something dictates at a steady clip and the race truly develops into a one-pace test from the front.

scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Outstays Leader
scenarios.trigger: If A Little Something's gallop is honest enough to set up a sustained battle from the home turn.
scenarios.body: If A Little Something's gallop is honest enough to set up a sustained battle from the home turn.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lates Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and leave closers with ground to make up in the straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and leave closers with ground to make up in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Falls, Errors Reshape Race
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or fallers disrupt the front-running pack and scramble the order.
scenarios.body: If jumping errors or fallers disrupt the front-running pack and scramble the order.

watchPoints.text: A Little Something — if it jumps cleanly to the third fence and has clear air, the uncontested lead could prove almost impossible to peg back at this manageable pace on fast ground.
White Riot — its jumping record (fall, pulled up) over fences needs monitoring early; a blunder at any of the first four fences would dramatically open the race up for the prominent group behind.
Citizen Jane — going-to-firm conditions have never featured in its form, and after an 807-day layoff a markets drift in the ring would be a telling signal that connections have reservations.

No Mean Feat — the 54-day break combined with the visor first-time headgear and a yard cold over 14 days creates a compound uncertainty flag; watch how it travels early to judge if there is any market confidence behind it.

Gore Point — Sam Twiston-Davies taking over the ride is a jockey-switch upgrade worth tracking; if it jumps fluently and travels sweetly just off the pace through the first mile, it is the horse most structurally placed to exploit the controlled fractions.

races.name: Racing TV Profits Returned To Racing Novices' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Back To Cali
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner with licence to make all at his own pace; John Joseph Hanlon's charge has been running over shorter trips on Soft/Heavy recently, and this step back up to 2m6f on Good to Firm is a fitness test after 84 days off — his style fit here is strong but his form return is modest (43543-).
runners_data.comment: Top of our figures here, and operating from a yard currently in good form — he finished third at Cork on his most recent outing; however, he has stamina to prove over today's trip, his best form has come on softer conditions than today's, and he returns from a lengthy absence.

runners_data.name: Slack Alice
runners_data.note: Won over 23f on Good ground last time out and has strong course-trip profile in her recent history; Sean Bowen's booking for Mickey Bowen's yard (T14: 2/14 in form) is a positive angle, and the visor is noted — a genuine hold-up type who should get an uncontested stalking position in this pace-light field.
runners_data.comment: Took a handicap with authority at Market Rasen last time off a 7lb lower mark than today, showing she is progressing — effective over staying trips and acts on good ground; a visor added here, and 7lb higher could test her, but she rates a genuine threat in this novice company.

runners_data.name: North Account
runners_data.note: Away for 386 days (last run flagged as a Pull-Up), and his last three form figures over Good ground show he fades badly in the finish; C A McBratney's yard is 0/5 in the 14-day window and the horse has a clear stamina-in-the-closing-stages concern that makes him hard to recommend at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Well held in hurdle starts to date and coming off an exit before the race properly developed in a point-to-point at Hexham, he has plenty to prove on current evidence and is difficult to make a compelling case for in this company.

runners_data.name: Vesalius
runners_data.note: True hold-up type whose best going form (sim: 0W1P from 7) came over similar conditions; Isabelle Ryder takes a 5lb claim which helps offset the low OR of 76, but this horse will likely race further off the pace than ideal given the crowded rear — the style displacement is worth bearing in mind when assessing his finishing chance.
runners_data.comment: Third in a hurdle earlier this season, he has shown some ability and cheekpieces are applied for the first time here; he failed to complete at Bangor-on-Dee last time, and a step up in trip could suit — yet he has something to prove on recent form before he can be called a reliable danger.

runners_data.name: Mc'flo
runners_data.note: Form figures of 65-896 tell a story of consistent mid-to-lower finishing, and on Good ground he averages around 7th from 10 runners; Jack Quinlan takes over and the horse may push forward into a more prominent pitch given the redistributed map — but his raw form makes a winning performance hard to project.
runners_data.comment: Lowest-rated on our figures and consistently held in her last five outings, she has shown limited ability so far; she has the trip handled and acts on decent ground, but needs significant improvement to be a factor here.

runners_data.name: Alex The Great
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's yard is active and in reasonable nick (T14: 9/51), and the tongue-tie is applied; a true hold-up horse who has been competitive at shorter distances on Good, but his history over the extended 2m6f trip is limited and his sim-going record (0W0P from 15) offers little encouragement for a place claim.
runners_data.comment: Sixth on handicap debut at Worcester last time without threatening, he steps up in trip today which could play to his strengths — effective at 2m on good ground, and tongue-tie applied for the first time; yet to score but this longer test may bring improvement.

runners_data.name: French Diablo
runners_data.note: The youngest in the field at four, carrying bottom weight (142lbs) on just three hurdles starts, with a pull-up last time out; the hood is worn and he's a genuine back-marker by instinct — Paddy Hanlon's 5lb claim helps, but limited experience over this far (22f ceiling in form) on a quick surface makes the step up in trip a significant query.
runners_data.comment: Making his handicap debut here with a first-time hood added, and the drop in weights could give him a better opportunity to show what he can do; yet to score over hurdles so far and failed to complete at Newton Abbot last time, he has considerable improvement to find.

races.paceDynamic: Back To Cali is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner novices' handicap hurdle over 2m6f at Stratford on Good to Firm ground, and with no rival likely to seriously dispute the lead, he should control the gallop from the outset at a tempo entirely of his choosing. The remainder of the field — Slack Alice, Vesalius, Mc'flo, Alex The Great, French Diablo, and North Account — are all natural hold-up or wait-and-see types, meaning Back To Cali can dictate a sustainable, uncontested pace that suits a horse with stamina rather than raw speed. Four of those hold-up types (Vesalius, Mc'flo, Alex The Great, French Diablo) are redistributed to midfield on the map because there are simply too many rearward runners to all settle at the back; in practice, Mc'flo and French Diablo are the most likely to push forward and achieve a prominent pitch, while the others will be forced to find their way through from further back than ideal. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a measured pace — strongly favours hold-up horses with the class and stamina to close over the final two flights, and riders able to judge their run from off the pace in a small, slowly-run field.

scenarios.title: Back To Cali Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Back To Cali is allowed to bowl along uncontested at a comfortable clip and the field settles tamely behind.
scenarios.body: If Back To Cali is allowed to bowl along uncontested at a comfortable clip and the field settles tamely behind.

scenarios.trigger: If Sean Bowen settles Slack Alice towards the rear and delivers a well-timed challenge between the last two hurdles.
scenarios.body: If Sean Bowen settles Slack Alice towards the rear and delivers a well-timed challenge between the last two hurdles.

scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Closers Shut Out
scenarios.trigger: If Back To Cali and one or two redistributed runners push the tempo higher in the back straight, stringing the field out.
scenarios.body: If Back To Cali and one or two redistributed runners push the tempo higher in the back straight, stringing the field out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Cavalry Fails to Fire
scenarios.trigger: If the small field produces a muddling, stop-start pace that scrambles the hold-up horses' ability to find clear daylight.
scenarios.body: If the small field produces a muddling, stop-start pace that scrambles the hold-up horses' ability to find clear daylight.

watchPoints.text: Back To Cali's tempo is the race-shaper — if Harry Skelton gets away unchallenged and sets a truly steady clip, the hold-up horses in behind will need a sustained gallop to close, so watch whether he quickens early in the back straight or dawdles.

Slack Alice is fitted with a visor for the first time — watch her keenness from the gate; if she over-races and burns her hold-up credentials early, the entire scenario built around her stamina advantage collapses.

With four horses all wanting to be rearward in a seven-runner field, watch the early positioning battle between Vesalius, French Diablo, Mc'flo and Alex The Great — whoever secures a clean, unobstructed midfield berth will have a meaningful advantage over those forced wide or pocketed.

North Account's 386-day absence and pull-up last time out makes him a significant safety flag — watch how he jumps the early hurdles, as a mistake or refusal would disrupt the following pack particularly if they are tightly grouped.

French Diablo's hood is a first-time application — monitor how he loads and whether he settles in the early stages, as a young, hood-wearing horse with limited experience could unsettle the small field if he idles or races erratically near the rear.

races.name: Every Race Live On Racing TV Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Bagheera Ginge
runners_data.note: OR 122 top-rated, Sam Twiston-Davies partners a mare with an excellent 14/15 record at good ground and three wins at similar trips; pure hold-up style means she needs the pace to be genuine — her chance improves if Nickelforce is pressed harder than expected, and the visor headgear is a positive flag.
runners_data.comment: A winner twice in his last five starts and comfortable at today's trip and going, he prefers to force the pace and is effective on a sound surface; inconsistent by nature and well beaten when stepped up in grade last time, but 1lb lower today offers marginally more favourable terms.

runners_data.name: Nickelforce
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner likely to bowl along at a controlled tempo, and Ben Case has hit form (1/3 in 14 days); his preferred trips look shorter than today's 2m6½f, which is the key question mark against what otherwise looks a strong style-fit for this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Dependably consistent with two wins in his last five starts, he powered clear by 9 lengths at Fakenham last time from a slightly lower mark — well suited to today's trip and a sound surface, he looks a solid proposition and must be respected in this small field.

runners_data.name: She Is For Me Boys
runners_data.note: Gavin Sheehan takes a prominent position that suits her progressive form (333-21 recently), and her good-ground figures (7/10) back up a live chance; the tongue-tie headgear is retained and Jamie Snowden's 1/9 in 14 days provides a mild flag, but the step back to this distance from her last two runs is the only minor unknown.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap at Worcester last time with a combination of front-running and cleaner jumping, racing from only 2lb higher today — she heads our figures comfortably and her pace-setting style suits a small-field test; tongue-tie added for the first time, though the 22-furlong trip tests the outer limit of her proven stamina range.

runners_data.name: Normofthenorth
runners_data.note: Trained by Alan Hill and returning after a staggering 1,123-day absence (36 previous points-form runs noted); a natural prominent type by inclination whose two runs on similar going both produced a place or win, but the extreme absence eclipses everything else and a fitness-free run should be expected rather than a serious challenge.
runners_data.comment: Landed a point-to-point by 15 lengths recently and returns under rules for the first time in nearly three years — his stamina at this trip is not in doubt and cheekpieces are added; the key question is how his pointing form will translate back into handicap company.

races.paceDynamic: Nickelforce is the confirmed front-runner here and, in a field of only four, is likely to control proceedings from the outset at a measured, sustainable gallop over 2m6½f on good-to-firm ground at Stratford. She Is For Me Boys is a genuine prominent racer who will likely sit close behind Nickelforce, meaning the two will jointly dictate an honest but not brutal tempo. Bagheera Ginge is a confirmed hold-up type who will settle in rear and look to make ground in the final circuit, while Normofthenorth — a natural prominent runner — has been redistributed to midfield on the map because She Is For Me Boys is more likely to claim that second position ahead of it; the field holds more prominent types than can all secure their natural slot, and She Is For Me Boys looks best placed to get the position. A controlled, front-running gallop with one genuine hold-up horse closing from off the pace favours prominent racers who can track the leader and pounce at the final few fences, rather than a single deep closer needing a strong pace to reel in fresh legs.

watchPoints.text: Nickelforce's preferred trip appears to be around 2m–2m1f based on its history — watch whether it begins to tie up after the second-last fence if the distance tests its stamina at this trip.
Normofthenorth has been off for 1,123 days and any early exuberance from this veteran at the start could compromise its race and disrupt the front pair's rhythm.

She Is For Me Boys and Nickelforce could race in close proximity for much of the trip — watch for any scrimmaging at early fences that may unsettle either runner given the small field and likely fast pace through the early part.

Bagheera Ginge is the hold-up horse in a race that may not generate enough pace to fully suit — watch whether Sam Twiston-Davies opts to position her closer than typical if the gallop appears too sedate on the far side of the course.
The going report confirms Good To Firm for this race (not Good as declared) — horses with a soft-ground profile or fitness concerns may find conditions sharper than they have recently encountered.

races.name: Racing Again Tomorrow Evening Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Basilette
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid recent form including a win and placed efforts on good and firm ground; tongue strap worn, 230 days off last time out (returned in form 16 days ago), and the 2m½f trip on good-to-firm suits her record of 12 similar-going runs with a win and seven places.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in her last five starts demonstrates she has the form to be competitive, effective over today's trip and going, with sharp tracks to her liking; however, her most recent outing was well below that level and cheekpieces are applied for the first time.

runners_data.name: Best Night
runners_data.note: David Pipe's five-year-old has a strong trainer who is in fine form (6 wins from 9 over 14 days) and has been placed four times in five hurdle runs on good ground, making her a strong candidate to travel prominently and capitalise on a controlled gallop; tongue strap worn, only 26 days since last run.
runners_data.comment: Second at Warwick on her most recent start and generally consistent of late; effective over 2m and acts on soft and good ground, but today's good-to-firm conditions may test her on the quicker side.

runners_data.name: Callin Baton Rouge
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type who races from the rear and relies on a strong gallop to deliver her finishing effort; 13 of 15 similar-going runs suggest she handles conditions, but a modest pace from the lone front runner is her primary threat.
runners_data.comment: Effective over today's trip and going, and racing below her last successful mark, she heads our figures as the most likely contender; yet to land a win in recent starts, but she briefly threatened at Southwell before tiring, suggesting this 16f trip could stretch her.

runners_data.name: Roarin' Success
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare in the care of Donald McCain whose recent form (5th last time) hasn't sparkled; trainer's 14-day record of 1 from 18 is modest, and without a strong gallop she will struggle to land a blow from off the pace on this flat Stratford track.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in her last four outings, she was held comfortably at Uttoxeter where the surface appeared quicker than ideal — today's good-to-firm conditions pose a similar test; tongue-tie applied for the first time, and while effective at this trip, there is more needed to trouble the principals.

runners_data.name: Lucy The Wire
runners_data.note: The confirmed front runner — rated OR 100 — but her style-fit tag (0.92) and the [STYLE_FIT] notation reflect that she is racing slightly out of her most comfortable role in a competitive handicap; three of five recent runs on good ground ended in placings, and if she bowls along unchallenged she will be hard to dislodge before the last.
runners_data.comment: Went desperately close on handicap debut at Kempton last time, beaten a neck off this very mark — a performance that suggests she remains competitive at this level; returning from a 98-day absence and effective around 2m, though today's quick surface may be on the firm side for her.

runners_data.name: Never Told Me
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien's seven-year-old is a prominent-style mares' hurdler with a fall last time out (the 'F' in form) that must be excused; tongue strap worn, five of six runs on similar going suggest she handles conditions and her consistency from mid-pack in similar grade makes her relevant.
runners_data.comment: Ranked second on our figures and effective over today's distance, she has the ability to be competitive; first-time tongue-tie applied, but the fall at Fakenham last time leaves something to prove, and she is yet to land a win in her last four starts.

runners_data.name: A Tickatickatiming
runners_data.note: Sheena West's eight-year-old travels prominently and has placed twice from seven runs on similar going; her form figures include a second last time and she handles the 2m½f trip, though her modest trainer record (0 from 2 over 14 days) and age are mild negatives.
runners_data.comment: Generally consistent over hurdles and effective at today's 2m trip on a sound surface, she is a solid contender on our ratings despite being yet to score in recent starts; she tired over a more testing distance at Fontwell last time, so this shorter trip could play to her strengths.

runners_data.name: Little Lady Lucy
runners_data.note: A five-year-old with two recent wins on good ground who races from hold-up; headgear (hood/p) worn and her record of 2 wins and 3 places from 7 similar-going runs is solid, though she is one of several hold-up types who will find it hard to reach her natural position at the rear of this field.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in her last five starts and thriving lately, she was narrowly denied last time off a lower mark than today — effective over today's trip and going, with cheekpieces added here; only a 2lb rise separates her from that near-miss, and she rates a genuine each-way threat.

runners_data.name: Driving Miss d'Azy
runners_data.note: Kim Bailey's five-year-old is a hold-up type whose recent form (6th, 7th, 8th) has been modest, and four of five runs on good ground have ended outside the frame; needs a strong pace to deliver her run and the slow-burn scenario does not suit her at all.
runners_data.comment: Consistently finishing out of the places in her last four starts, she has all to prove here; a first-time hood is applied today and she handles the trip and going, but held comfortably at Huntingdon last time when needing the run, this looks a tough assignment.

runners_data.name: Shing Shilla
runners_data.note: Adrian Sexton's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse whose true place is at the rear, but the crowded nature of this field means she has been pushed into a midfield mapping position she would not naturally occupy; 13 of 15 similar-going runs tell you she handles conditions, but the style displacement and a 0 from 6 trainer run means her chance is materially tempered.
runners_data.comment: Placed in a hurdle at one point but well beaten in each of her last four starts since, she is yet to score and would need marked improvement to figure in this company; effective at the trip and carries a relatively light weight, but recent evidence offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Jukebox Annie
runners_data.note: A natural closer who has been redistributed to midfield on the map because there are too many hold-up types for all to sit at the back — Claire Hitch's seven-year-old is unlikely to secure her ideal position and the only scenario that suits her requires a contested pace that this race is not expected to produce; one win from 13 similar-going runs tells its own story.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Newton Abbot on her most recent outing after a break, where she held her position until tiring near the finish — effective at the trip and on a sound surface, she handles today's going, but needs more to be a serious factor in this competitive field.

runners_data.name: Northern Rose
runners_data.note: Gary Hanmer's six-year-old is a prominent-to-lead type who has been placed six times in 15 runs on similar going and was racing just 13 days ago; her consistent proximity to the pace makes her a potential factor if she travels well, but the 8th and 9th in her last two suggest her form is not at its peak.
runners_data.comment: Quick return to Stratford where she tired after setting too strong a gallop on her latest visit; tongue-tie and cheekpieces applied together for the first time, and in good form in the run-up to that outing — effective at the trip and going, though she remains yet to land a win.

runners_data.name: Miss Fedora
runners_data.note: Nick Scholfield's seven-year-old is a hold-up horse naturally suited to a strong gallop, but the race map has her in midfield because the rear of the field is over-subscribed; 68 days since her last run and a recent form string featuring pulls-up (P) and refusals make her hard to trust, and her style displacement compounds the concern.
runners_data.comment: Returning after a 68-day absence, her hurdles form is modest at best — keen in her latest run at Taunton and well held, with a pull-up and a refusal also among her recent outings; she handles the trip and going, but her reliability over hurdles is questionable and fences remain her better sphere.

runners_data.name: Hollysaway
runners_data.note: Ella Pickard's five-year-old is tagged as fading in the finish and is another hold-up type mapped to midfield due to congestion at the rear; only three career runs, a modest record (0 wins, 0 places), and a tendency to weaken late make her the least attractive runner in the field under this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Lowest-rated on our figures and well beaten in each of her last three starts, she has all to prove here; a wind operation preceded her most recent run at Worcester, where she offered minimal response and finished well held, leaving genuine questions over her ability to compete.

races.paceDynamic: Lucy The Wire is the sole confirmed front runner in this 14-runner mares' handicap hurdle over 2m½f on Good to Firm ground at Stratford, and with no genuine challenger for the lead she is likely to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than being harried into setting a scorching tempo. Behind her, Basilette, Best Night, Never Told Me, A Tickatickatiming and Northern Rose are the prominent-style runners who will attempt to race in the slipstream, creating a bunched pack through the early and middle stages. The field does contain more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear — Shing Shilla, Jukebox Annie and Miss Fedora are genuine closers mapped to midfield simply because there is no room for them at the back of such a competitive field, meaning their true finishing positions may not reflect their natural patterns. A single, unhurried leader dictating a fair but unforced gallop on fast ground over this trip is a recipe that historically rewards horses who travel prominently behind the pace and produce a clean jump at the last — prominent-to-midfield runners with sound jumping and proven form on good-to-firm going are best placed here, while the redistributed closers will find it harder to mount a genuine late challenge if the pace is only modest.

watchPoints.text: Lucy The Wire's gallop control is the central variable — watch whether Jonathan Burke allows her to bowl along in front or whether any prominent horse challenges her for the lead early, as that will determine whether the pace is genuinely compressed or begins to string the field out.

Basilette's 230-day absence (returned 16 days ago) and 168lbs top weight alongside her age (7) mean fatigue in the closing stages is a real risk despite her recent placed effort — watch her jumping from three out.

Best Night's hold on a prominent pitch will be tested immediately at the start given the number of runners also seeking a prominent position — if she gets crowded out in the early stages she could find herself racing further back than ideal, which would undermine her chance.

The cluster of hold-up horses (Shing Shilla, Jukebox Annie, Miss Fedora, Hollysaway) all being pushed out of their natural positions means the closing stages may look messy — watch for horses appearing to finish with running but having nowhere to go through the pack on the flat Stratford straight.

Little Lady Lucy's hood headgear and sharp recent form (two wins from three on good ground) mean she is worth tracking from the outset — if she manages to settle towards the rear, she is one of the more genuine late runners in a field where most closers are not true closers.
